objective: T-20260930-11 (corridor C1): registry direction dir:cross_sectional_gap_fade (refuted at T-20260929-32 after per-stock costs of 18-28 bp per side). Measure, for the >=$20M dollar-volume tiers, the gross edge of the same gap-fade picks on official opening and closing auction prices: E_off = E_bar + mean paired difference Delta, Delta = r_off - r_bar from a 400-row stratified sample, versus the frozen bar of 8 bp/day per unit position.
target_regime_and_horizon: Benchmark window 2024-01-08 to the last day of the local panel; one-day hold (official open in, official close out), long and short legs; stress window 2016-05-02 to 2023-08-31 reported on daily bars only. This is a measurement of a price-definition effect, not a claim about a market regime; a continue verdict would only license a full preregistration, not trading.
existing_solution_comparison: Published: Concretum (2026) reports the gap fade at CAGR about 98% / Sharpe 2.08 gross of costs and itself warns that commissions, impact and borrow change the picture; Goyal-Jegadeesh-Wu (JFQA 2026) say closing auctions are the cheapest venue and opening auctions illiquid. Why not enough: no source measures the official auction prices that a gap-fade book would actually trade at, per stock, against the daily-bar open/close that our backtests use; the parent T-32 cost model is estimated from close/high/low (Abdi-Ranaldo), a proxy that an auction-priced execution might bypass. Reuse: T-32 picks, price hygiene and easy-to-borrow proxy are imported, not rebuilt.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether daily-bar open equals the official opening auction price (Alpaca daily bars are built from trades with conditions that exclude Q and M prints, so the first eligible trade defines the bar open) and whether the paired difference moves the gross edge above the 8 bp bar in the >=$20M tiers. Not measured here: opening-auction price impact of our own orders (Goyal-Jegadeesh-Wu stress tier), borrow, fees, and Alpaca paper opening-auction fill reliability (45 of 50 orders expired on 2026-09-15).
negative_experiments_checked: oc research directions check gap fade (2026-09-30): dir:cross_sectional_gap_fade refuted at T-20260929-32 (gross short-leg edge +11.5 bp/day, Sharpe 1.33, placebo 100% lost to the real book; realistic 2x-per-side cost plus borrow -38.5 bp/day; K1 and K2 reject in all 8 cells, including the >$100M tier). Its reopen_if names exactly an execution path with materially lower effective spread than the Abdi-Ranaldo estimate, which is what auction prices would test; dir:overnight_intraday_gap_retail_pwb refuted (different mechanism: fixed overnight hold); dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal refuted (ETF-level). The T-32 report was read for selection rule, hygiene and tiers.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: This step charges no costs: it measures gross edge on official auction prices. Selection and price hygiene follow T-32 (signal z = (open/prev_close - 1)/sigma21; long dv21>=$1M, close>=$5, history>=60 days, 10 lowest z; short dv21>=$5M and dtc percentile<0.90, 10 highest z; sanitize_price_matrices defaults; split-like trigger sessions dropped). Official price rule frozen in hypotheses.md: open = trade with condition Q else O, close = M else 6, from Alpaca historical SIP trades (data.alpaca.markets only). Full-book costs (fees, JFQA opening-auction impact stress, borrow by tier) belong to the follow-up preregistration; Alpaca paper cannot verify the opening leg reliably.
stop_condition: Frozen before any official auction price is fetched. Continue to a full preregistration only if E_off_T2T3 >= 8 bp/day per unit position, where E_off = E_bar + mean Delta per tier and leg, pooled over T2 and T3 by row count with the long and short legs equally weighted. Close the intraday single-stock gap-fade line if E_off_T2T3 < 8 bp. A tier whose missing rate exceeds 20% is reported no_conclusion and cannot support continue. No change to tiers, sample sizes, seed, the 8 bp bar or the price rule after seeing results.

sources.claim: Goyal, Jegadeesh and Wu (JFQA 2026, NYSE and Nasdaq 2012-2021): closing auctions carry about 10% of daily volume and have lower price impact than the continuous market for all stocks except Nasdaq microcaps; opening auctions are illiquid (opening auction volume is 5%-10% of closing auction volume, under 1.5% of ADV after 2015) and carry the largest price impact; long/short anomaly portfolios cost 17-41 bp per year, 9-21 bp excluding microcaps in closing auctions.
sources.market_and_period: NYSE and Nasdaq stocks, 2012-2021, TAQ plus exchange auction files
sources.applicability: Frames the second cost item (opening-auction impact) that this step does not measure and that the full preregistration must stress; supports entering at the open only in small size or by limit orders.
sources.limitations: Costs are annualized for low-turnover anomaly portfolios, not a daily-turnover book; price impact is measured for institutional-size orders, not the effect of the auction price vs daily-bar open, which is what this step measures.
sources.independent_replication: Working-paper version SSRN 4300417 (2022); no independent replication found.

sources.claim: UTP Plan specification (Sept 2026 edition) sale-condition table: Q = Market Center Official Open, O = Opening Prints, M = Market Center Official Close, 6 = Closing Prints; direct data recipients should use the Q value as the official market center opening value.
sources.market_and_period: Nasdaq-listed (tape C) UTDF feed, current specification
sources.applicability: Fixes the official-price rule: official open = trade with condition Q, else O; official close = M, else 6.
sources.limitations: Nasdaq (UTP) specification; the CTA equivalent for NYSE and NYSE American tapes A and B uses the same letters but is a separate document not fetched here; the check5 step verifies the codes against real trades.

sources.claim: Alpaca Market Data FAQ: the rules that decide which trades update a bar depend on tape (A, B NYSE; C Nasdaq; O OTC), the trade conditions and the bar type; a trade can have more than one condition and the strictest rule applies; the table lists per-condition whether open/close, high/low and volume are updated.
sources.market_and_period: Alpaca Market Data API, SIP feed, current documentation
sources.applicability: Tells us the daily-bar open and close are built from a rule set that can exclude Q and M prints, so official auction prices can differ from the daily-bar open/close, which is the paired difference measured here.
sources.limitations: The FAQ is a rendered web page; the exact per-condition table is read from the page text; there is no versioned date on the page, the published date recorded is the fetch-time year.

sources.claim: Lou, Polk and Skouras (JFE 2019): for 14 trading strategies, profits are earned entirely overnight (reversal and a variety of momentum strategies) or entirely intraday, typically with profits of opposite signs across the two components.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks, CRSP, decades of daily open/close data
sources.applicability: Confirms that split of returns between close-to-open and open-to-close is a stable feature; the gap-fade signal trades the intraday leg after the overnight gap.
sources.limitations: Uses first-print or official open depending on the data set and no transaction costs; not a tradability study.
sources.independent_replication: Subsequent literature (Akbas et al. 2022, cited by Concretum) reports similar patterns.

sources.claim: Abdi and Ranaldo (RFS 2017): a bid-ask spread estimator from daily close, high and low prices gives the highest cross-sectional and average time-series correlations with the TAQ effective spread when quote data are unavailable, and the most accurate estimates for less liquid stocks.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks, TAQ effective spread benchmark, 1993-2012
sources.applicability: Justifies the parent experiment T-32 per-stock spread cost that this step tries to bypass with auction prices.
sources.limitations: Estimator accuracy is highest for monthly averages, noisy for single stock-days.

sources.claim: Nagel (RFS 2012, NBER WP 17653): returns of short-term reversal strategies proxy for the returns to liquidity provision; the expected return is strongly time-varying and predictable with the VIX, rising sharply in turmoil.
sources.applicability: Interprets the gap-fade edge as liquidity provision, which competes with the spread we would have to pay; edge concentrates in high-VIX periods.
sources.limitations: Monthly/weekly reversal, not intraday gap fade; paid liquidity means the edge and the cost are linked.
sources.independent_replication: Replicated in follow-up papers on reversal and liquidity.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: scripts/run_t20260930_11_gap_fade_auction.py: picks (rebuild benchmark-window picks, E_bar by tier and leg, 400-row stratified sample under run_capped 1.2G), check5 (hand-check condition codes on 5 rows), fetch (Alpaca historical trades, opening window 09:29-09:45 ET and closing window 15:59-16:10 ET, resumable, 3 requests per second), analyze (paired Delta, bootstrap 90% interval, E_off).
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: E_off_T2T3 >= 8 bp/day per unit position with T2 and T3 missing rates each at most 20%; then the follow-up full preregistration (auction book, JFQA impact stress, borrow by tier) is licensed.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: E_off_T2T3 < 8 bp/day: the intraday single-stock gap-fade line is closed and the cause recorded (price definition or thin margin). A tier with missing rate above 20% is no_conclusion, not a pass.
